aria: Animated recap of the Magic's 107 to 99 home win over the Bucks: Franz Wagner's steal and Euro-step layup with 42 seconds left that made it 104 to 94, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Wagner's 35 points, 12 assists and 9 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Magic won, and the next game at Boston.
notes: Box score from the Magic's 107–99 win over the Milwaukee Bucks at the Kia Center on Nov 13, 2026, an NBA Cup group game, from the Covers.com and StatMuse box scores (they match on every player), with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News, CBS 58 and Spectrum News 13), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker and The Ticket), Yahoo Sports, Magic on SI and ClutchPoints. All 107 Orlando points and all 99 Milwaukee points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 52–37 Orlando at the half and 84–72 after three (Covers.com; Field Level Media). Biggest leads: Orlando 20 (65–45 in the third, Field Level Media), Milwaukee 1 (Covers.com, StatMuse). Points in the paint, fast-break points, assists and free throws are from Covers.com; points off turnovers and second-chance points are from StatMuse. Records and ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Friday's games.

Wagner had 35 points on 13-of-22 shooting, 12 assists and 9 rebounds, one rebound short of his first career triple-double (AP). He had 18 in the first half (Field Level Media), 12 of them in the second quarter (Yahoo Sports), and it is his fourth straight 30-point game (AP; ClutchPoints). Desmond Bane made 6 of 10 threes. It is Orlando's third straight win and its first at home this season (AP; Magic on SI); Milwaukee has lost nine straight (AP) and went 18 of 31 at the line. Orlando plays at Boston on Monday at 7:00 PM ET (ClutchPoints; Yardbarker).

How it ended: Wagner's turnaround hook with about six minutes left made it 94–81 and gave him 30 (AP; Field Level Media). Kyle Kuzma's driving layup cut it to 94–84 at 4:45, and Tyler Herro's three free throws after a flagrant foul on Bane made it 102–94 at 1:36 (Field Level Media; StatMuse play log).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Wagner's steal and Euro-step layup with 42 seconds left, which made it 104–94 (AP: "Wagner stole the ball and used a Euro-step layup to give Orlando a 104-94 advantage"; Field Level Media: "Wagner then iced the game with a layup on the other end"; StatMuse's play log has the layup at 0:42). The steal and the Euro-step aren't animated; it is drawn as the template's plain drive to the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Orlando Magic or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Wagner's listed 6-foot-10 and 220 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to a reported 7-foot wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Orlando's home white with No. 22 (Basketball-Reference). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
